Various [[History of Christianity#Early_Christianity_(c._27_–_fourth_century)|early Christian writers]] wrote [[gospel]]s and other books, some of which were canonized as the [[Development of the New Testament canon|New Testament canon developed]]. The [[Apostolic Fathers]] were prominent writers who are traditionally understood to have met and learned from [[Jesus]]'s personal [[Disciple (Christianity)|disciples]]. The [[Church Fathers]] are later writers with no direct connection to the disciples (other than the claim to [[apostolic succession]]). [[Christian apologetics|Early Christian apologists]] tried to defend Christianity against [[Criticism of Christianity|its critics]], especially the [[Ancient Greek philosophy|Ancient Greek]] and [[Ancient Roman philosophy|Roman philosophers]]. Dates given, if not otherwise specified, are of their writings or [[Episcopal see|bishopric]], not of their lives.

*[[Paul of Tarsus]], "Apostle to the Gentiles", earliest New Testament author 45~65
*[[Four Evangelists]], traditionally identified as the authors of the [[canonical gospels]] 60~125
*[[Ignatius of Antioch|Ignatius]], bishop of Antioch, apostolic father 68~107
*[[Marcion of Sinope]], evangelist and theologian, founder of [[Marcionism]], published the first known [[Biblical canon|canon]] of the New Testament,<ref name="Ehrman 2005">{{cite book |last=Ehrman |first=Bart D. |author-link=Bart D. Ehrman |year=2005 |orig-year=2003 |title=Lost Christianities: The Battles for Scripture and the Faiths We Never Knew |chapter=At Polar Ends of the Spectrum: Early Christian Ebionites and Marcionites |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=URdACxKubDIC&pg=PA103 |location=[[Oxford]] |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |pages=103–112 |doi=10.1017/s0009640700110273 |isbn=978-0-19-518249-1 |lccn=2003053097 |s2cid=152458823}}</ref> 85~160
*[[Clement of Rome]], bishop of Rome, apostolic father 88~101
*[[Papias of Hierapolis|Papias]], bishop of Hierapolis, apostolic father 110~130
*[[Polycarp of Smyrna]], bishop of Smyrna, apostolic father 110~160
*[[Aristides of Athens]], apologist ~120
*[[Justin Martyr]], church father ~165
*[[Melito of Sardis]], bishop of Sardis, ~180
*[[Irenaeus]], [[bishop of Lyon]], disciple of Polycarp, apologist 180~202
*[[Origen|Origen of Alexandria]], 185~254, [[Neoplatonism|Neoplatonist]], controversial during his lifetime, posthumously condemned at the [[Second Council of Constantinople]] in 553
*[[Tatian]], pupil of Justin Martyr, ascetic theologian ~185
*[[Athenagoras of Athens]], philosopher, apologist ~190
*[[Polycrates of Ephesus|Polycrates]], bishop of Ephesus, excommunicated by [[Pope Victor I|Victor I of Rome]] over the [[Easter controversy]] ~196
*[[Montanus]], self-proclaimed prophet and founder of [[Montanism]], last quarter of 2nd century CE
*[[Tertullian]], church father, apologist, first Christian writer in Latin, later a Montanist 197~230
*[[Hippolytus of Rome|Hippolytus]], church father, sometimes termed the first [[Antipope]], reconciled with the church and died a martyr 217~236
*[[Cyprian]], bishop of Carthage, martyr 218~258
*[[Clement of Alexandria]], church father, Bishop of Alexandria ~220
*[[Antipope Novatian|Novatian]], a rigorist and Antipope in 251
*[[Dionysius of Alexandria|Dionysius]], patriarch of Alexandria, pope of the Coptic Orthodox Church 248~264
*[[Paul of Samosata]], bishop of Antioch, [[Adoptionism|adoptionist]], condemned at 269 [[Synods of Antioch|Council of Antioch]]
*[[Athanasius of Alexandria]], c. 297~373, patriarch of Alexandria, defender of the [[Trinitarianism|Trinitarian doctrine]]
*[[Donatus Magnus]], bishop of Carthage, (+355), leader of the [[Donatism|Donatists]] from 313
*[[Lactantius]], apologist ~317
*[[Arnobius]], apologist ~330
*[[Eusebius]], wrote ''History of the Church'' ~325
*[[Augustine of Hippo]], 354-430, Latin church father, wrote ''Confessions'' and ''City of God''
